47-year-old women with metastatic cervical carcinoma.
She first noticed a swollen cervical LN in 10/2022, that on FNA was diagnosed as squamous cell cancer. This was followed by limited left neck dissection in 12/2022 (32 of 43 LN positive). Imaging with widespread disease in neck and pelvis. She received 6 cycles of carbo/taxol/pembro followed by pembro maintenance. Recurred after 4mo on pembro and resumed carbo/taxol/pembro. 
Cancer Type ID testing resulted with 96% probability of cervical origin. Upon progression in 02/2024 she started tisotumab vedotin and received 9 cycles. Progression of iliac adenopathy and received RT to pelvis 10-12/2024. 
In 12/2024 then progression with significant hepatic disease, some pulmonary disease and received carbo/taxol with avastin for 6 cycles. During her last cycle she had a platinum hypersensitivity reaction, with facial edema and erythema and chest pressure. She now progressed 05/05/2024 on CT scans. 
She now reports abdominal distension and early satiety with some RUQ discomfort. Weight stable. Some fatigue but does not nap daily, until recently was still playing tennis. Mild neuropathy of fingertips and toes. Denies CP, SOB, N/V/D, edema, rashes, vision changes.
Today�s labs are unremarkable. 
She presents for screening/consultation.

Her main symptoms are related to her cervical mass with pelvic discomfort. 
ECOG PS=0, without major intercurrent adverse events from prior therapies.

48yo F with metastatic stage IV cervical squamous cell cancer
Initial Diagnosis: stage Ib1 cervical cancer dx 1/23/2022 positive for HR-HPV on PCR, treated with simple hysterectomy, specimen with parametrial invasion so given adjuvant chemoRT
Metastatic Diagnosis: Lung lesions found on CT scan 2/15/2023, biopsy confirmed recurrence of p16+ SCC consistent with PD-L1+ cervical cancer primary on 2/22/2023
Metastatic Disease Treatment Course:
Cisplatin + paclitaxel + pembrolizumab + bevacizumab x 6 cycles followed by pembrolizumab maintenance 3/2023 – 5/2024. Progression diagnosed in RUL lung lesion on PET-CT 5/20/2025
Treatment holiday 6/2024 - 8/2024
Tisotumab vedotin 9/1/2024 – 6/15/2025. Rescan CT scan 7/8/2025 showed new liver lesions. Biopsy and CARIS testing showed no actionable mutations, HPV-16 DNA+, HLA-A*02:01+.
Home oncologist starting palliative topotecan while patient looking for clinical trial options. Working full-time, ECOG 1.

Initial Diagnosis: stage IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma diagnosed 12/20/2024 with primary left tonsillar mass, cervical lymph nodes, and 2 subcentimeter lung nodules
Treatment course:

8/2025 – 9/2025 single agent pembrolizumab, lung nodules remained stable but discontinued due to immune-mediated pneumonitis
11/2025 – present palliative single-agent cetuximab
Bilateral lung lesions are stable on first follow-up scan after starting cetuximab but circulating levels of HPV-16 DNA increasing, home oncologist referring for clinical trial options. Retired teacher, ECOG 0, active exercise. HLA-A*02:01+ on outside HLA serotyping testing.

Metastatic Diagnosis: new liver lesions on CT scan 9/2024. Biopsy right liver lobe lesion confirmed p16+ squamous cell carcinoma consistent with anal primary on 9/13/2024
Metastatic Treatment Course:

Nivolumab 1/2025 - 7/2025 with progression in old and new liver lesions. Repeat liver biopsy for CARIS testing shows HLA-A*02:01, no actionable mutations
8/2025-11/2025 treatment on clinical trial with novel immunotherapeutic agent GIGA-564, progressive disease in liver on CT scan 11/5/2025. Self-employed works 20 hours per week and homemaker, ECOG 1. Outside oncologist referring for consideration of another clinical trial, may start mFOLFOX if no viable trial option in next month.

HLA-A*01:01 positive, CT83+. ECOG 1.

This is a 75-year-old male with metastatic penile squamous cell carcinoma which was initially diagnosed as localized disease (10/2023) via partial penectomy (2.5cm moderately differentiated, invading corpus spongiosum, negative martins, positive for lymphovascular invasion, p16 IHC negative, pT2Nx). He was later found to have an enlarging right inguinal lymph node with biopsy proven squamous cell carcinoma (12/2023). He received 2 cycles of TIP and restaging PET demonstrated worsening bilateral inguinal and right pelvic sidewall nodules consistent with metastatic disease. He then received chemoradiation with 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin (2/12/24-4/20/24). Restaging imaging demonstrated progressive lymphadenopathy and new disease in the chest (08/02/2024).

This is a 55-year-old gentleman with metastatic urachal adenocarcinoma to the lungs who was diagnosed with previously localized urachal adenocarcinoma status post partial cystectomy and urachal remnant excision (1/1/2023) with pathology notable for adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous features and microinvasion of muscularis propria. The patient received modified FOLFIRINOX for which he eventually discontinued oxaliplatin given peripheral neuropathy. He was found to have a left upper lobe mass measuring 2cm with subsequent biopsy proven metastasis (8/03/2025).

This is a 31-year-old female with a history of sickle cell trait who was diagnosed with SMARCB1-deficient renal medullary carcinoma. She initially presented to the Emergency Department (01/30/25) with 2 weeks of left lower quadrant and left flank pain, where imaging revealed a large heterogeneous renal mass (greater than 8cm) with concern for metastatic disease in the retroperitoneal space and lungs. She underwent an IR-guided left kidney core biopsy (03/03/25) with pathology demonstrating renal medullary carcinoma. The patient’s PET imaging demonstrated metabolically active lung metastasis, a left renal mass, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Her main symptoms included severe left flank pain warranting uptitration of oxycodone at her most recent Medical Oncology visit.

This is a 73-year-old female with past medical history notable for hyperlipidemia, medullary sponge kidney with recurrent nephrolithiasis s/p percutaneous nephrolithotomy for staghorn calculus 2017, who was diagnosed with T1 small cell carcinoma of the bladder with a concurrent high-grade urothelial carcinoma component. She was diagnosed with localized disease 11/20/21 and received 3 cycles of neoadjuvant cisplatin and etoposide (1/31/22-4/4/22) with a complete clinical response. She then later developed recurrent muscle-invasive small cell carcinoma almost 11 months later (noted on 2/2/24 TURBT) with metastatic disease to the liver (core biopsy 3/5/24). Bone imaging demonstrated concern for a possible L3 osseous lesion. She progressed following 2 additional cycles of cisplatin and etoposide (4/5/24-5/2/24). She then received 9 cycles of pembrolizumab (5/29/24-2/2/25 - held intermittently after cycle 3 secondary to pneumonitis toxicity). The patient has had persistently negative ctDNA since 9/1/2024; however recent MRI of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated clear progression of liver metastases (02/16/2025).

This is a 40-year-old male diagnosed with large cell neuroendocrine tumor of the bladder (stage IIIB; TxN3) which was initially diagnosed 10/31/2023. He received 6 cycles of carboplatin, etoposide, and atezolizumab with partial response following 3 cycles, and progression of disease following 6 cycles. The patient was later found to have an incidental meningioma (found on imaging during workup for dizziness) that was up to 9.0 cm. He underwent subtotal resection 01/2024. Given the patient was found to have an enlarging hypermetabolic urachal mass and left external iliac lymph nodes on imaging, he underwent robotic assisted partial cystectomy with extended pelvic lymph node dissection (3/25/2024). He was then found to have disease recurrence in the left pelvis contributing to left hydronephrosis and had a left percutaneous nephrostomy tube placed (6/10/2024).

This is a 69-year-old male with metastatic small cell neuroendocrine tumor of the bladder. Initially, the patient was found to have localized disease (8/30/23). He also had metastatic thyroid cancer to the lung status post thyroidectomy and RAI (1995). The patient on subsequent imaging was found to have lung lesions and underwent a left lower lobe wedge (9/01/2024). He received 4 cycles of platinum and etoposide (completed 12/2024) followed by a right ureterectomy (pT3N0). The patient received 4 cycles of adjuvant nivolumab (2/2025); however, recent PET/CT 06/2025 demonstrated new liver metastases with biopsy proven metastatic disease (08/03/2025).

This is a 81-year-old male with a history of remote prostate cancer (cT1NxMx, Gleason 3+3=6) who received Lupron and brachytherapy (1999), then diagnosed with metastatic clear cell adenocarcinoma of the urethra who was found to have disease in his lymph nodes (pelvis, retroperitoneum, right axilla). The patient presented initially with disease invading the periurethral fibromuscular and adipose tissue with tumor focally present at the periurethral resection margin (after radical cystectomy and urethrectomy). The patient received adjuvant radiation therapy; however, he had a biopsy proven recurrence in his right inguinal lymph node (07/23/2025). The patient then received 8 cycles of FOLFOX and ultimately following treatment, demonstrated radiographic progression of disease (09/24/25).

This is a 75-year-old female with de novo metastatic urethral clear cell adenocarcinoma to lung with a urethral mass in situ diagnosed in September 2025, on a background of a urethral diverticulum (diagnosed 2002) and a long history of recurrent UTIs. Other co-morbidities are PMH HTN, uterine fibroids. She received 6 cycles of CAPOX with progression of disease.

This is a 75-year-old male with peripheral neuropathy of unknown cause, mucinous adenocarcinoma of the urethra. Initially, he was diagnosed following hospitalization for bilateral ureteral stent obstruction and creatinine above 15. Following bilateral stent replacement, he underwent TURBT which was notable for poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (signet ring cells). It was difficult to determine whether the cancer originated from the genitourinary tract or gastrointestinal tract; however, the patient underwent radical cystectomy with pelvic exenteration (pT4pN2R1). He was determined to have genitourinary primary and received 1 dose of FOLFOX (which he could not tolerate). He presented with progression of disease following adjuvant chemotherapy, with measurable lymphadenopathy in the mediastinum.

This is a 55-year-old male active skier, ECOG 0, who was diagnosed with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder who received 2 cycles of TIP (end date: 01/12/2025) with concurrent palliative RT to bladder. He demonstrated response to his lung lesions; however, developed complications such as radiation pneumonitis, bacteremia and pulmonary emboli. He then received treatment with immune-checkpoint inhibitor pembrolizumab for 5 cycles total (2/6/25-6/20/25); however, developed progressive disease in his lungs. He then received 3 cycles of therapy on SMART (sacituzumab govitecan). The patient clinically progressed and was found to have Horner’s syndrome (on the right) secondary to his disease.

This is a 58-year-old male with recurrent urachal adenocarcinoma metastasized to the left iliac lymph node and abdominal wall who was originally diagnosed in January of 2022. He had a negative colonoscopy in February 2022. The patient underwent robotic partial cystectomy (6/20/22) and was ultimately found to have a metastatic recurrence in the bladder dome and peritoneum (12/6/2024). He received 4 cycles of FOLFOX and then underwent debulking surgery (with partial cystectomy and HIPEC (04/20/2025). The patient ultimately was found to have biopsy proven recurrence of peritoneal masses (12/2025).

This is a 36-year-old male diagnosed with high risk metastatic mixed germ cell tumor to lung (75% choriocarcinoma, 20% seminoma) s/p R radical orchiectomy (11/2024). He progressed following VIP and BEP (dates unknown). The patient then received gemcitabine and oxaliplatin for a few cycles prior to autologous stem cell transplant. His chemotherapy associated side effects have been minimal, with trace numbness at his fingertips. Guardant 360 Tissue testing (11/5/24) demonstrated Her2 3+. The patient was then initiated on trastuzumab deruxtecan (12/1/25-). Recently, the patient developed worsening right upper rib pain and was found to have elevation of his tumor markers (bHCG above 20,000). He was later discovered to have brain metastases which were radiated. PET/CT demonstrated interval increase in size of the patient’s lung lesions.

A 26-year-old single woman who is currently in graduate school presents with worsening depressed mood, marked anhedonia, impaired concentration, disrupted sleep, anxiety, sensitivity to criticism, and passive suicidal ideation without plan, intent, or past attempts. Her current depressive episode can be traced back about 5 months ago when she felt increasing pressure to increase her productivity towards her degree coincided with a family member receiving a cancer diagnosis. She restarted sertraline (up to 150mg/day), which has helped in the past, but has only had marginal improvement in her mood symptoms during this episode. Her current psychiatrist added Ambien 10mg and Abilify 5mg at bedtime to try to help with sleep, but they were not very helpful. She also takes clonazepam 0.25mg PRN (takes about 3x a week for anxiety), but is willing to stop taking that and the sertraline (it’s not working much anyway) for participation in research. 
She first experienced depression as a teenager, and at the time saw a school counselor a few times per month. During college, she did well in classes, but states she had one or two depressive episodes lasting at least 3 months per year. She saw a therapist through student health during these times, who referred her to a psychiatrist for treatment during the ‘worst episode’ as a senior when she learned her parents were getting divorced; this episode lasted about 6 months. At that time, she started bupropion XL up to 300mg/day but felt too jittery and switched to sertraline after a couple of months. This helped with depressed mood, sleep, and anxiety at the time. After graduation, she stopped this medication and successfully applied to graduate school.  She denies any history of psychosis, manic-like symptoms, trauma-related symptoms (other than frequently thinking about a time she was bullied in high school for being a ‘goth’), and has no history of inpatient admissions, ECT, or TMS. She has not tried ketamine or esketamine before. 
Medically, she is generally healthy. She has well-controlled mild asthma treated with as-needed albuterol (needs it more during allergy season). She sees an OBGYN annually and has a PCP in her hometown and does not think she has ever had abnormal labs.  She was active with a dance team until two years ago when graduate studies intensified and still tries to swim 3x a week. She drinks alcohol socially a few times per month, and smoked marijuana a few times socially in college. She smoked marijuana regularly for a few months to try to help with ‘anxiety’ but denies any use in the last few years. She denies any other drug use. She currently lives with two roommates near her school in a large Midwest city, and identifies her roommate, her mom, and her brother as her closest supports.

A 52-year old married man working as an accountant presents with long-standing history of long recurrent depressive episodes. He first started dealing with depression in his 20’s, especially with feeling worthless and finding like ‘the world slowed down’. He was never able to put his finger on any particular reason that would precipitate an episode, but they would last for months. A few years ago, he was doing worse at work and missing many days; at his wife’s suggestion he tried esketamine over 4 weeks and responded well and was able to go back to work regularly and stay on escitalopram 20mg/day since that time. He denies any history of suicidal ideation, and states “I could never do that to my family, it’s a sin anyway”. He denies any history of mania, psychotic symptoms, or major traumas (any more than anyone else). 
He has a history of two mild concussions, (once in a car accident, another time while playing basketball and getting elbowed) but states he was just “woozy” and never lost consciousness either time. He states he has had both knees repaired from torn ligaments from playing basketball (played competitively in college until the last surgery) but denies any metal in the body. He takes atorvastatin for hyperlipidemia, and a stable dose of an alpha-1 blocker (tamsulosin) for symptoms of mild BPH but denies symptoms of obstructed voiding.  He has had periods of hypertension but has managed it well with lifestyle interventions with the support of a cardiologist and swears by ‘intermittent fasting’. He denies any history of coronary artery disease. His last lab results from an annual physical with his PCP were all unremarkable. He shares a case of beer with a friend every weekend, but denies any history of dependence, drinking causing problems, or substance abuse.  He does not smoke tobacco and denies ever trying illicit drugs. “I have thought about those magic mushrooms though for my depression.”  He states his wife is his biggest support and ‘just wants me to get well and get the real me back’.

A 66-year-old widowed woman presents with a 3 month episode of depression, marked by persistent sadness, feeling alone, loss of interest in her volunteer work and social club, guilt about burdening her children, poor appetite with 5lb weight loss (over 3 months), and thoughts “it would be easier to just not wake up”. She thinks she was also given lithium while she was admitted in her twenties but didn’t like how it made her feel and stopped taking it after discharge. She denies any history of psychosis or mania. She states she has “a lot of weird dreams that get pretty scary” and endorses a difficult upbringing, but denies trauma-related symptoms like recurrent nightmares, intrusive thoughts, or flashbacks. She states she hasn’t stuck with any psychiatrist very long, but has had the same therapist for 20 years.  She has been taking mail ordered ketamine troches and thinks they are helpful. Medically, she has well-controlled hypothyroidism (treated with levothyroxine, now has normal TSH), osteoarthritis managed with acetaminophen, and hyperlipidemia treated with simvastatin.  She has severe claustrophobia and does not think she can do the optional MRI component of the study, but would still like to try to do as much as she can for the study. 
In terms of social history, she lives alone, but often has one or many of her grandkids to take care of after school or for a weekend. Her 4 adult children live near her and she sees them regularly, but she feels like she is ‘mostly a babysitting service’ for them, and hates when she has to ask one of her kids for help with things, and does not feel like she can talk to them about her mood or other problems. She retired after her husband died 10 years ago (major heart attack), and tries to volunteer 20 hours a week in her community at the library tutoring underprivileged children for free, and organizing events for her church including the monthly tea time and rummage sale.
